answer: Score each identity by what it costs to fake, not by what it claims. A submission needs five auditors from unrelated subnets, each re-deriving the work alone and posting the hash before seeing peers. Two auditors disagreeing voids the submitter's epoch and pays the pair a small fee for the catch. Concrete case: 200 farm accounts need 1,000 distinct auditor slots per epoch, more than the network can seat before dawn, so half the queue expires under a willow of ungraded work while honest submissions clear the terrace first. Replication cost climbs faster than identity count.
